## Tool Information

| Item | Details |
|---|---|

## Huang's Data Guide

I downloaded the Quartz *Bad Data Guide* and asked Claude to help me turn its
roughly sixty items into a checklist I would actually use.

> **Me:** 我已經下載下來了 幫我完成這個做頁並把我的清單存在 F:\…\Class2
>
> *(I have downloaded it. Help me finish this page and save my checklist in the Class 2 folder.)*

**What Claude contributed:** the organising idea of grouping the items by **who
can fix the problem** rather than by symptom, the Tier 1 fifteen-minute subset,
and the English wording.

**What is mine:** the decision to make the guide personal rather than a summary
of the original, and the two domain sections at the end — gridded weather
reanalysis and medical imaging — which come from the data I actually work with
in my own research. Claude could not have supplied those items; I told it what
goes wrong in those datasets.

## Review of *Teaching to See*

I watched the 37-minute film and wrote my reactions in Chinese. Claude turned
them into the English review.

The observations are mine:

- The **Beethoven poster**, where the letter E is drawn together with the lines
  of a musical staff — and the fact that I did not see the staff at first.
- The **signature exercise** and the thick/thin variation produced by a broad pen
  held at a fixed angle.
- **Steve Jobs** and the calligraphy class behind the Macintosh typefaces.
- The **symmetry of the Roman alphabet**, and that every letter has to be adjusted
  so the spaces stay even.

After reading Claude's first draft I replaced three sections with my own text and
had Claude work those in rather than paraphrase them:

- **Section 1** — rewritten by me.
- **Section 2** — I supplied the Holmes quotation on the eye and the hand.
- **Section 4** — my own point that **geometric accuracy and optical accuracy do
  not coincide**, which became the section on why a letter that is mathematically
  correct can still look wrong.

## Why I Used AI Here

To produce readable English at the length the course expects, in a week when I
was also preparing for an exam. The reading, the viewing, and the judgements are
mine; the drafting and the structure are shared.
